quote: Yeah. No. There's not a pocket cost during upfront fees.
stewart_read: Rep confirms a financing claim (no out-of-pocket cost) without clarifying the mechanism, which is closer-tier financial content.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have simply been affirming a true baseline fact (no upfront fee) rather than engaging the financing mechanism itself.
coaching_implication: Redirect financing specifics to the specialist: 'the exact numbers and financing options are exactly what my specialist will walk you through' instead of repeating the no-cost framing.

quote: But she's saying there's no out of pocket costs at all.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a strong pre-sold anchor (friend's referral, no-cost belief) and the rep answers it directly rather than using it to build curiosity about his own specific numbers.
coaching_implication: Rep could pivot: 'that's exactly why we build a custom design off your actual bill — let's see what your numbers look like' to turn belief into curiosity rather than confirming a secondhand claim.

quote: I mean, it depends. Like, in the summer, I'll pay, you know, like, $70. In the winter, it can be closer to $15,200.
stewart_read: Bill amount is captured but the rep moves straight to 'K. Great job' without flipping the seasonal swing into emotional leverage against the utility.
coaching_implication: Flip line missing: 'so your bill basically doubles every winter regardless — that's exactly the kind of unpredictability solar removes.'

quote: And do you guys come out and inspect, like, the roof and everything and make sure that's in a good condition before you do any install?
stewart_read: Rep answers directly and confidently ('100%... we do a site survey') rather than deferring to the specialist, but the answer stays procedural, not technical, so it's a mild rather than severe scope creep.
alternative_hypothesis: This is a legitimate verify-adjacent process question the setter is expected to know, not true scope creep.
coaching_implication: Fine as handled — flag only if rep starts detailing structural specifics beyond 'we do a site survey.'

quote: And I know you said you meant, that you've you've had some designs before. How long ago was that when you lastly didn't do it?
stewart_read: Customer disclosed a prior solar design a year ago, and rep only asks how long ago, never which company or why it didn't move forward.
coaching_implication: Ask 'what company was that with, and what stopped it from moving forward?' to surface competitive context per verify.prior_designs.

quote: I don't know if tomorrow will work for me.
stewart_read: First real scheduling resistance of the call; rep offers Friday/Saturday alternatives rather than conceding to a vague callback.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep could have lost the appointment entirely here if he hadn't offered alternatives immediately.
coaching_implication: This is the correct move — alternative_offered kept the close alive; hold this up as a positive example for the floor.

quote: One of my friends actually actually told me that there was someone, like, soliciting in her neighborhood
stewart_read: Referral-driven interest with a pre-sold friend as the source is a strong qualifying signal — customer arrived warmer than average.
coaching_implication: Rep should have dug deeper into this reason (probe.interest_in_solar depth) rather than immediately shifting into address confirmation — missed opportunity to deepen the emotional anchor before it was 'checked off.'
